Token usage Reasoning tokens count toward both your output-token limit and billed completion tokens: Output-token limit : max_tokens (Chat Completions) and max_output_tokens (Responses API) cap reasoning tokens plus visible output tokens combined. If the model spends most of the budget on reasoning, the visible response may be truncated. Set the limit high enough to accommodate both. Billing : Reasoning tokens are billed at the same rate as visible output tokens. The usage breakdown reports them separately as completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens (Chat Completions) or output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens (Responses API). Higher reasoning_effort produces more reasoning tokens, which means longer latency and higher cost. Use the lowest level that gives you acceptable results. At "max" , reasoning tokens make up a larger share of output_tokens than at lower efforts, so set the output-token limit generously. When to reach for reasoning Higher reasoning effort helps with multi-step problem solving: proofs and calculations, complex code generation, architecture trade-off analysis, and task planning and sequencing. sources.text: Subscriptions - Meta Model API Skip to content Subscriptions Table of contents With a Muse Code subscription, you pay a flat monthly rate for usage of Muse Code , instead of paying per token. Subscription benefits and availability may vary by region. Available benefits will be shown to you during onboarding before you subscribe. About subscriptions To sign up for a Muse Code subscription, you will need a Meta Account. Using your Meta Account, you can create an associated Meta Model API account and sign up for a subscription. The subscription applies to the Muse Code API key that is automatically connected in the Muse Code CLI onboarding process. This credential is for use with Muse Code only. Any additional API keys you create under your Meta Model API account will be billed through pay-as-you-go . You must be 18 or the age of majority in your country to subscribe. Your subscription is subject to the Meta Subscription Terms of Service (opens in new tab) , and your use of Muse Code and the Meta Model API is governed by the Meta Model API Terms of Service and the Meta Model API Acceptable Use Policy . How Meta uses your content — the prompts, code, files, and context you send, plus the model responses you get back — depends on whether Contributor mode is on in your settings, and is described in the Meta Model API Terms of Service . There are 4 subscription plans available for Muse Code: Everyday Usage Access to the Muse model family Send 10-50 prompts every 5 hours, including image and video uploads Use voice mode Get access to web search High Usage Everything from the Everyday Usage plan 5x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan More multimodal inputs Power Usage Everything from the High Usage plan Access to the most powerful Muse models 20x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan Early access to new features Higher file uploads Maximum Usage Everything from the Power Usage plan 80x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan Contributor mode Muse Code subscriptions default to Contributor mode. In Contributor mode, you get more usage from your plan in exchange for letting Meta use your content to train future Meta models. Contributor mode is a setting in Muse Code, and you can turn it off at any time, at which point your future content is not used to train Meta models (unless you turn it back on in your settings). Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full are each available in either mode on the plans that include them. For the models each plan includes, see Muse Wonder availability . Choose pay-as-you-go or a subscription Muse Code supports 2 ways to pay for usage: Pay-as-you-go : billed per token consumed with your Meta Model API key. See billing and plans . Subscription : a flat monthly rate (see the plans above). It works only through the Muse Code CLI while signed in with your Meta Model API account. If you reach your plan's usage limit, you can upgrade to the next plan, or wait until your limit refreshes. If you are on the Maximum Usage plan, you must wait for your limit to refresh. Usage through any additional API keys you create is billed pay-as-you-go. Subscribe Sign in to Muse Code with your Meta Model API account on dev.meta.ai , then subscribe through Accounts Center: Go to Subscriptions in Accounts Center (opens in new tab) . Select Muse Code , then choose a plan and complete checkout. On success, you will see a confirmation screen with a link to your receipt and the option to Manage your subscription . Change or cancel your plan Manage your plan from Manage your subscription on the Subscriptions page in Accounts Center (opens in new tab) . From an interactive session, type /upgrade to open Accounts Center in your browser. Upgrade : A plan upgrade takes effect immediately. You will be charged a prorated amount for the rest of the current billing cycle. Downgrade : A plan downgrade takes effect at the start of your next billing cycle. You will keep your current plan's usage limit until the next billing cycle. Cancel : From Accounts Center, go to Manage your subscription and select Cancel subscription . Your subscription stays active until the end of the current billing cycle, then you lose access to all benefits. Cancel at least 24 hours before your next billing date to avoid future charges. What happens when your subscription ends A subscription ends one of 2 ways: you can cancel it (see Change or cancel your plan ), or Meta can revoke it. Revocation is different from cancellation. When your subscription is revoked, you lose access immediately instead of at the end of your billing cycle. Meta may revoke a subscription for various reasons, including: Payment failure : your payment method fails and you have no backup payment method on file. Policy violation : your account violates the Model API terms , Meta's Community Standards (opens in new tab) or Meta Subscription Terms of Service (opens in new tab) . Account deletion or deactivation : deleting your account cancels the subscription immediately. Deactivating your account keeps the subscription active for 30 days. If you don't reactivate within that window, Meta revokes it. Loss of eligibility : for example, your account no longer meets the age requirement, or you move to a restricted territory. To subscribe again after a revocation, your account must meet the eligibility requirements in About subscriptions . Billing cycle Your subscription renews automatically each month on the date you first subscribed. If that date doesn't exist in a given month (for example, the 31st in a 30-day month), you're charged on the last day of that month instead. Manage your payment method and view billing history from Accounts Center (opens in new tab) . No refunds for canceled subscriptions : if you cancel your subscription, you won't receive a credit or refund unless required by law. Next steps Set up sign-in and pay-as-you-go billing in authentication and billing . Start your first session in the overview . sources.text: Muse Wonder: A Frontier Model For Personal & Professional AI Agents Skip to main content Loading demo Play Researchers introduce Muse Wonder and discuss its capabilities. Play Show captions for Researchers introduce Muse Wonder and discuss its capabilities. Show captions Mute Researchers introduce Muse Wonder and discuss its capabilities. Mute Researchers introduce Muse Wonder and discuss its capabilities. playback position 0:00 of 0:00 00:00 / 00:00 A frontier model that leads on personal and professional agents Today, we’re excited to introduce the Muse Wonder series with Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, our most capable models that deliver state-of-the-art performance on personal and professional agentic tasks. Together, they mark the next step on our scaling ladder and a major leap toward personal superintelligence. Muse Wonder brings together Active Memory and Active Focus to keep track of what matters to you and work diligently toward what you want to accomplish. Muse Wonder is available today through the Meta Model API and Muse Code , and Muse Wonder Full is available today for Muse Code subscribers. Muse Wonder will soon power experiences in Muse , and will roll out first to subscribers. Muse Wonder will also power artifact generation and processes that require more intelligence. And in the future, we’ll be using Muse Wonder to develop specialized models that we can bring to everyone using Muse. Scaling Toward Personal Superintelligence Fourteen months ago, we began a ground-up overhaul of our artificial intelligence efforts. In that time, we’ve gone from rebuilding our stack from first principles to pushing the frontier. When we introduced Muse Spark , we outlined our approach to predictable, rigorous scaling. Today’s release builds on that work across pretraining and reinforcement learning, delivering our most capable models yet. Trained at our gigawatt-scale Prometheus data center, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full bring together the work of teams across Meta to deliver frontier capabilities for complex tasks at work and in everyday life — another step toward bringing personal superintelligence to the billions of people who use our products. Frontier Capabilities Model Highlights The Muse Wonder series achieves state-of-the-art results across key benchmarks for personal and professional agents, memory, and coding. The full results below compare Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full with other frontier models across a broad evaluation suite. For more details about our evaluations, see our report . The results above provide a broad view of the models’ performance. We now take a closer look at four areas central to their work on real-world tasks: domain expertise, Active Memory, Active Focus, and frontier coding. Domain Expertise Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full apply specialized knowledge to problems people encounter at work and in daily life, from understanding a lease to making sense of financial or health information. Our evaluations include tasks in law, finance, and health that test this ability. Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB), for example, requires models to work with source documents and follow detailed instructions to produce legal work products. Active Memory One of the most critical steps towards useful personal and professional agents is reliable memory. Models need to remember what matters and recognize when earlier information becomes relevant. We call this Active Memory : carrying important context about you across conversations and actively retrieving the details relevant to the task at hand. Active Focus Using that context to complete a task also requires sustained effort. Active Focus describes how Muse Wonder continues working toward a challenging goal: trying alternative approaches, working through blockers, and adapting to new information. Along the way, it asks for clarification when needed and checks in before taking important actions. We evaluate focus through FocusBench and sustained execution through SWE-Marathon, which tests work on long-running software projects. Frontier Coding Coding brings these capabilities together. Building software requires tracking requirements, making changes across a codebase, and working through repeated cycles of testing and revision. Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full deliver frontier coding performance, supporting projects from small applications to complex software. We trained both models on diverse, long-running tasks to help them sustain progress across this process. Kitchen Game Wellness Support Insurance Claim Kitchen Game Loading demo Muse Wonder builds a playable 3D kitchen game from customizable image inputs. Capabilities That Generalize Two models often have similar benchmark scores, yet one seems to handle a much wider range of unfamiliar tasks. That’s what complaints of “benchmaxxing” and praise for “big model smell” both get at: a breadth of capability that popular benchmarks in a few domains can’t fully capture. To quantify this mismatch, we investigate how performance on tasks targeted during post-training relates to performance on unfamiliar tasks as we scale test-time compute. The plot below compares Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse Wonder Full, with each point denoting performance at a distinct reasoning effort. The horizontal axis shows the model’s score on a composite representative of the tasks we focused on during post-training (“in-distribution”). The vertical axis shows the average score on a set of tasks we did not target during post-training (“out-of-distribution”). Both of our models improve similarly on out-of-distribution tasks as we scale test-time compute. But given its in-distribution performance, Muse Wonder Full performs even better on unfamiliar tasks than the Muse Spark 1.3 trend would predict. sources.text: Muse Wonder Model Card This card describes the Muse Wonder models, the evaluations we ran, and the limits of that testing. 1. The models Name Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full Model Provider Meta Platforms, Inc. or Meta Platforms Ireland Limited Website dev.meta.ai Date of Release October 12, 2026 Modalities Input: text, image, video, audio Output: text Languages The model was trained on multilingual training data, with substantial representation across worldwide languages. Context Length 1M tokens at inference Contact https://dev.meta.ai/support 2. Intended uses The Muse Wonder models are intended for commercial and research use, with particular strengths in personal and professional agentic tasks. Th ... ... Overall Methodology ● Models and configurations. Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full results are generated with max reasoning effort. We compare with GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Opus 5.5 at max reasoning effort. For controlled internal coding comparisons, every model uses the same benchmark-specific harness. External coding results retain the harness or agent product used by the reporting vendor or model provider, and that source is identified below. ● Evaluation and score selection. We preserve each benchmark’s tasks, inputs, grading, and primary metric as closely as possible. Where a comparable third-party or provider-reported result exists, we use it; otherwise we use the highest of our internally validated run, self-reported score, or official leaderboard score. Benchmark names link to official leaderboards where available. Model refusals receive zero credit and remain in the denominator rather than being dropped. Material departures from the official setup are noted below. ● Competitor-model results. Internally generated competitor runs use common settings where practical but remain best-effort: prompts, tools, and runtime may not be optimally tuned for proprietary models. Per-benchmark details Personal and Professional Agents ● Personal Superintelligence Index (PSI). PSI is an internal composite of seven personal and knowledge-work evaluations: Agents’ Last Exam, AutomationBench-AA, FocusBench, JobBench, GDP.pdf, VBT, and DRACO. ● Harvey LAB-AA. Harvey LAB-AA is Artificial Analysis’s version of Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark, in which agents produce legal work products from matter documents and an Artificial Analysis judge panel checks each deliverable against task-specific criteria. We report version 1.1, which adds hallucination checks. The result sou ... MemoryBench. MemoryBench is an internal benchmark that tests how accurately a model can recall critical information across long, complex multi-turn conversations of 64K to 100K tokens that span several individual facts, with distractor conversations and injected turns that conflict with or later update the target details. An LLM judge scores each answer against weighted, question-specific rubric criteria. ● Verifiable Browsing Task (VBT). VBT is an internal agentic web-browsing evaluation in which models answer list-style information-seeking questions, written as realistic user requests, using browser search, open, and find tools. ● Deep Research Accuracy, Completeness, and Objectivity (DRACO). DRACO, from Perplexity, is a deep-research benchmark of 100 complex, multi-domain questions. ... DeepSWE v1.1. DeepSWE is a long-horizon software-engineering benchmark with 113 tasks across 91 repositories and five languages. Handwritten functional and regression tests grade each task, and the primary metric is pass@1. The scorecard uses Datacurve’s third-party results for Muse Wonder, Muse Wonder Full, and Claude Opus 5.5, and OpenAI’s provider-reported result for GPT-6 Astra. For Claude Fable 5.1, we use the result reported in Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.1 system card. ● SWE-Marathon. SWE-Marathon is an ultra-long-horizon software-engineering benchmark of substantial projects graded by executing project tests. The primary metric is pass@1. Abundant AI is the result source for all models. Its leaderboard results for GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 use Codex and Claude Code, respectively, so this row is not a controlled common-harness comparison. Muse Wonder Full was reported with xhigh reasoning effort. ● ProgramBench. ProgramBench evaluates whether an agent can reconstruct a complete program in a clean-room environment. Each submission is compiled and graded by a hidden behavioral test suite, with internet access disabled after setup. All compared models use mini-swe-agent. The primary metric is the percentage of rollouts passing at least 95% of tests. General ● AA Intelligence Index v4.3. AA Intelligence Index v4.3 is Artificial Analysis’s composite index. It combines evaluations Artificial Analysis runs independently, including GDPval-AA, AA-Briefcase, AutomationBench-AA, GDP.pdf, Terminal-Bench 4.0, SciCode, AA-LCR, AA-Omniscience, CritPt, and Humanity’s Last Exam, into a single score. The result source is Artificial Analysis, and the primary metric is the index score. ... 6. Considerations and Limitations Muse Wonder is a technology that carries known and unknown risks. Testing conducted to date has not covered, and could not cover, all scenarios. Limitations 1. The model may produce inaccurate, biased, or objectionable responses to user prompts. 2. While optimized for agentic tasks, the model may still make errors in multi-step reasoning, particularly in novel scenarios not well represented in training data. 3. Visual and spatial reasoning, especially 3D tasks, remains a known limitation. Validate performance for applications that depend on precise spatial understanding. 4. The model has not been evaluated on all languages contained in the pre-training data. Performance may degrade on languages outside the strongly supported set. 5. Performance can vary with quantization, serving configuration, prompts, tools, and the agent harness. 6. The model is not intended to be used by individuals under the age of 18. Deployers are responsible for ensuring that any risks associated with such use by individuals ... under the age of 18 have been fully assessed and appropriately mitigated, and that such use complies with all applicable laws. Muse Wonder's use is subject to the restrictions and conditions in the applicable terms of use, including the Meta Model API Terms of Service (https://dev.meta.ai/legal/terms-of-service), Meta Model Acceptable Use Policy (https://dev.meta.ai/legal/acceptable-use-policy), and Muse Supplemental Terms of Service (https://muse.ai/terms). Responsible Use Developers should conduct their own evaluation of whether the model is appropriate for their deployment, with assessments tailored to their specific applications and proposed languages. Concept Details Billing unit Claude Consumption Unit ( CCU ) CCU price $0.01 per CCU (fixed; discounts apply at token-to-CCU conversion, not to the CCU price) Conversion Token usage rated in USD at standard per-model, per-feature rates (same as Claude API pricing ), then converted to CCUs at $0.01 per CCU Billing cadence Hourly metering to the Azure Marketplace; monthly invoices Payment model Arrears only (postpaid); no prepaid credits Discounts Applied as fewer CCUs metered Tax Pre-tax metering; Azure Marketplace handles tax Cost visibility Azure Cost Management shows aggregated CCU Inference geography  Deployments hosted on Azure can use the US Data Zone Standard deployment type, which keeps inference within the United States. This is equivalent to inference_geo: "us" on the Claude API and applies the same 1.1x pricing multiplier. See Data residency for details. Feature-specific pricing  Prompt caching  Prompt caching reduces costs and latency by reusing previously processed portions of your prompt across API calls. Instead of reprocessing the same large system prompt, document, or conversation history on every request, the API reads from cache at a fraction of the standard input price. There are two ways to enable prompt caching: Automatic caching: Add a single cache_control field at the top level of your request. The system automatically manages cache breakpoints as conversations grow. This is the recommended starting point for most use cases. Explicit cache breakpoints: Place cache_control directly on individual content blocks for fine-grained control over exactly what gets cached. Prompt caching uses the following pricing multipliers relative to base input token rates: Cache operation Multiplier Duration 5-minute cache write 1.25x base input price Cache valid for 5 minutes 1-hour cache write 2x base input price Cache valid for 1 hour Cache read (hit) 0.1x base input price (0.025x on Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1; 0.05x on Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5) Same duration as the preceding write Cache write tokens are charged when content is first stored. Cache read tokens are charged when a subsequent request retrieves the cached content. A cache hit costs 10% of the standard input price, which means caching pays off after one cache read for the 5-minute duration (1.25x write), or after two cache reads for the 1-hour duration (2x write). On Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, a cache hit costs 2.5% of the standard input price ($0.25 USD per million tokens). On Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5, a cache hit costs 5% of the standard input price ($0.20 USD per million tokens on Claude Opus 5.5, $0.10 USD on Claude Sonnet 5.5). These multipliers stack with other pricing modifiers, including the Batch API discount and data residency. For implementation details, supported models, and code examples, see Prompt caching . Data residency pricing  For Claude 4.6 and later models, specifying US-only inference through the inference_geo parameter incurs a 1.1x multiplier on all token pricing categories, including input tokens, output tokens, cache writes, and cache reads. On Claude Haiku 5.5, the multiplier also applies to the higher prices for prompts over 100,000 tokens (see Long context pricing ). Global routing (the default) uses standard pricing. This applies to the Claude API (first-party) and Claude Platform on AWS. On Claude in Microsoft Foundry, the same 1.1x multiplier applies to deployments that use the US Data Zone Standard deployment type (see Inference geography ). Partner-operated platforms (Bedrock and Google Cloud) have independent regional pricing. See Bedrock and Google Cloud for details. Earlier models do not support the inference_geo parameter and always use standard pricing; requests that include the parameter on these models return a 400 error. For more information, see Data residency . Fast mode pricing  Fast mode , in research preview, provides significantly faster output for Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Opus 5, and Claude Opus 4.8 at premium pricing. Fast mode pricing applies across the full context window, including requests over 200k input tokens. Fast mode is available on the Claude API (first-party) only; it is not available on Claude Platform on AWS or partner-operated cloud platforms. See Fast mode . Fast mode pricing stacks with other pricing modifiers: Prompt caching multipliers apply on top of fast mode pricing Data residency multipliers apply on top of fast mode pricing Fast mode is not available with the Batch API . For more information, see Fast mode . Batch processing  The Batch API allows asynchronous processing of large volumes of requests with a 50% discount on both input and output tokens. Long context pricing  Claude 4.6 and later models (except Claude Haiku 5.5) and Claude Mythos Preview include the full 1M token context window at standard pricing. (A 900k-token request is billed at the same per-token rate as a 9k-token request.) Prompt caching and batch processing discounts apply at standard rates across the full context window. Claude Haiku 5.5 is priced by prompt length: a request whose prompt is over 100,000 tokens pays higher prices. A request's prompt length counts all of its input tokens, including cache reads and cache writes. Each request is priced on its own: a request over the threshold pays the higher prices even when part of its prompt is a cache hit, and earlier requests keep the prices they were billed at. Model pricing and Batch processing list both sets of prices. Tool use pricing  Tool use requests are priced based on: The total number of input tokens sent to the model (including in the tools parameter) The number of output tokens generated For server-side tools, additional usage-based pricing (for example, web search charges per search performed) Client-side tools are priced the same as any other Claude API request, although server-side tools can incur additional charges based on their specific usage. The additional tokens from tool use come from: The tools parameter in API requests (tool names, descriptions, and schemas) tool_use content blocks in API requests and responses tool_result content blocks in API requests When you use tools , the API also automatically includes a special system prompt for the model that enables tool use. The number of tool use tokens required for each model is listed in the following table (excluding the additional tokens listed earlier). Note that the table assumes at least 1 tool is provided. If no tools are provided, then a tool choice of none uses 0 additional system prompt tokens. Model Tool use system prompt tokens Name Tool choice Token count Claude Opus 5.5 For long-running agentic coding and knowledge work auto , none 286 tokens Claude Sonnet 5.5 The best combination of speed and intelligence auto , none 286 tokens Claude Haiku 5.5 For high-volume, latency-sensitive tasks such as classification, extraction, and routing auto , none 286 tokens any , tool 406 tokens  Additional models Claude Opus 5 auto , none 286 tokens any , tool 406 tokens Claude Opus 4.8 auto , none 290 tokens any , tool 410 tokens Claude Opus 4.7 auto , none 675 tokens any , tool 804 tokens Claude Opus 4.6 auto , none 497 tokens any , tool 589 tokens Claude Opus 4.5 auto , none 496 tokens any , tool 588 tokens Claude Opus 4.1  auto , none 313 tokens any , tool 315 tokens Claude Opus 4  auto , none 313 tokens any , tool 315 tokens Claude Sonnet 5 auto , none 354 tokens any , tool 474 tokens Claude Sonnet 4.6 auto , none 497 tokens any , tool 589 tokens Claude Sonnet 4.5 auto , none 496 tokens any , tool 588 tokens Claude Sonnet 4  auto , none 313 tokens any , tool 315 tokens Claude Haiku 4.5 auto , none 496 tokens any , tool 588 tokens Claude Haiku 3.5  auto , none 264 tokens any , tool 355 tokens These token counts are added to your normal input and output tokens to calculate the total cost of a request. For current per-model prices, refer to the model pricing section. For more information about tool use implementation and best practices, see Tool use . Specific tool pricing  Bash tool  The bash tool definition adds the following input tokens to your request. This is in addition to the per-model tool use system prompt that applies whenever any tool is present. Model Additional input tokens Claude 4.7 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview 325 tokens Claude 4.6 and earlier models 244 tokens Additional tokens are consumed by: Command outputs (stdout/stderr) Error messages Large file contents See tool use pricing for complete pricing details. Code execution tool  Code execution is free when used with web search or web fetch. When web_search_20260209 (or later) or web_fetch_20260209 (or later) is included in your API request, there are no additional charges for code execution tool calls beyond the standard input and output token costs. When used without these tools, code execution is billed by execution time, tracked separately from token usage: Execution time has a minimum of 5 minutes Each organization receives 1,550 free hours of usage per month Additional usage beyond 1,550 hours is billed at $0.05 USD per hour, per container If files are included in the request, execution time is billed even if the tool is not called, because files are preloaded onto the container Code execution usage is tracked in the response: { "usage" : { "input_tokens" : 105 , "output_tokens" : 239 , "server_tool_use" : { "code_execution_requests" : 1 } } }  Text editor tool  The text editor tool uses the same pricing structure as other tools used with Claude. It follows the standard input and output token pricing based on the Claude model you're using. In addition to the base tokens, the following additional input tokens are needed for the text editor tool: Tool Additional input tokens text_editor_20250728 (Claude 4.7 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview) 974 tokens text_editor_20250728 (Claude 4.6 and earlier models) 745 tokens See tool use pricing for complete pricing details. Web search tool  Web search usage is charged in addition to token usage: { "usage" : { "input_tokens" : 105 , "output_tokens" : 6039 , "cache_read_input_tokens" : 7123 , "cache_creation_input_tokens" : 7345 , "server_tool_use" : { "web_search_requests" : 1 } } }  Web search is available on the Claude API for $10 per 1,000 searches , plus standard token costs for search-generated content. Web search results retrieved throughout a conversation are counted as input tokens, in search iterations executed during a single turn and in subsequent conversation turns. Each web search counts as one use, regardless of the number of results returned. If an error occurs during web search, the web search will not be billed. Web fetch tool  Web fetch usage has no additional charges beyond standard token costs: { "usage" : { "input_tokens" : 25039 , "output_tokens" : 931 , "cache_read_input_tokens" : 0 , "cache_creation_input_tokens" : 0 , "server_tool_use" : { "web_fetch_requests" : 1 } } }  The web fetch tool is available on the Claude API at no additional cost . You only pay standard token costs for the fetched content that becomes part of your conversation context. To protect against inadvertently fetching large content that would consume excessive tokens, use the max_content_tokens parameter to set appropriate limits based on your use case and budget considerations. Example token usage for typical content: Average web page (10 kB): ~2,500 tokens Large documentation page (100 kB): ~25,000 tokens Research paper PDF (500 kB): ~125,000 tokens Computer use tool  Computer use follows the standard tool use pricing . When using the computer use tool: Toolset definition overhead: Declaring computer_toolset_20260801 with its default members adds about 4,500 input tokens to a request (about 4,590 on Claude Sonnet 5 and about 4,520 on the other supported models), which covers the member tool definitions and the tool use system prompt. Disabling zoom with configs removes about 410 of those tokens. The exact count for a request is reported in the response usage , and you can estimate it in advance with the token counting endpoint . Earlier tool versions: The following figures apply to the computer_20251124 and computer_20250124 tool versions, not to computer_toolset_20260801 : System prompt overhead: 466–499 tokens added to the system prompt Tool definition: about 735 input tokens per tool definition (measured with computer_20250124 ) Additional token consumption: Screenshot and zoom images returned in tool results, billed as image input (see Vision pricing ) Tool execution results returned to Claude  If you're also using bash or text editor tools alongside computer use, those tools have their own token costs as documented in their respective pages. Browser use tool  Browser use follows the standard tool use pricing . When using the browser use tool: Toolset definition overhead: Declaring browser_toolset_20260801 with its default members adds about 6,600 input tokens to a request (about 6,670 on Claude Sonnet 5 and about 6,610 on the other supported models), which covers the member tool definitions and the tool use system prompt. Enabling all four optional members adds about 880 tokens, and disabling members with configs reduces the count. The exact count for a request is reported in the response usage , and you can estimate it in advance with the token counting endpoint . Additional token consumption: Screenshot and zoom images returned in tool results, billed as image input (see Vision pricing ) Text tool results returned to Claude, such as accessibility trees, page text, and console or network entries  If you also use the computer use tool, bash tool, text editor tool, or your own tools alongside browser use, those tools have their own token costs as documented on their respective pages. Claude Managed Agents pricing  Claude Managed Agents is billed on two dimensions: tokens and session runtime. Tokens  All tokens consumed by a Claude Managed Agents session are billed at the rates shown in Model pricing . Prompt caching multipliers apply identically. Web search triggered inside a session incurs the standard $10 per 1,000 searches. On Claude Platform on AWS , session token and runtime charges convert to Claude Consumption Units at the standard rate. Fast mode premium pricing applies when an agent's model.speed is set to "fast" . The data residency multiplier also applies: when an agent's model.inference_geo is pinned to "us" , tokens consumed by sessions running that agent are billed at 1.1x the standard rates, the same multiplier that applies to US-only inference on the Messages API. The following Messages API modifiers do not apply to Claude Managed Agents sessions: Modifier Why it doesn't apply Batch API discount Sessions are stateful and interactive. There is no batch mode. Cloud platform pricing Not available on partner-operated cloud platforms. Session runtime  SKU Rate Metering Session runtime $0.08 per session-hour running status duration Runtime is measured to the millisecond and accrues only while the session's status is running . Time spent idle (waiting for your next message or a tool confirmation), rescheduling , or terminated does not count toward runtime.  Session runtime replaces the code execution container-hour billing model when using Claude Managed Agents. You are not separately billed for container hours on top of session runtime. Worked example  A one-hour coding session using Claude Opus 5 that consumes 50,000 input tokens and 15,000 output tokens: Line item Calculation Cost Input tokens 50,000 × $5 / 1,000,000 $0.25 Output tokens 15,000 × $25 / 1,000,000 $0.375 Session runtime 1.0 hour × $0.08 $0.08 Total $0.705 If prompt caching is active and 40,000 of the input tokens are cache reads: Line item Calculation Cost Uncached input tokens 10,000 × $5 / 1,000,000 $0.05 Cache read tokens 40,000 × $5 × 0.1 / 1,000,000 $0.02 Output tokens 15,000 × $25 / 1,000,000 $0.375 Session runtime 1.0 hour × $0.08 $0.08 Total $0.525 Additional pricing considerations  Cost optimization strategies  When building agents with Claude: Use appropriate models: Choose Haiku for simple tasks, Sonnet for most production workloads, and Opus for the most complex reasoning Implement prompt caching: Reduce costs for repeated context Batch operations: Use the Batch API for non-time-sensitive tasks Monitor usage patterns: Track token consumption to identify optimization opportunities  For high-volume agent applications, contact the enterprise sales team for custom pricing arrangements. Rate limits  Rate limits vary by usage tier and affect how many requests you can make: Start tier: Entry-level limits for getting started Build tier: Increased limits for growing applications Scale tier: Highest standard limits for production workloads For detailed rate limit information, see Rate limits . For limits beyond the Scale tier or custom pricing arrangements, contact the sales team . Volume discounts  Volume discounts may be available for high-volume users. These are negotiated on a case-by-case basis. Standard usage tiers use the pricing shown in Model pricing Enterprise customers can contact sales for custom pricing Academic and research discounts may be available Enterprise pricing  For enterprise customers with specific needs: Custom rate limits Volume discounts Dedicated support Custom terms Contact the sales team at sales@anthropic.com or through the Claude Console to discuss enterprise pricing options. Billing and payment  Billing is based on actual monthly usage All payments are in USD Credit card and invoicing options available Usage tracking available in the Claude Console Frequently asked questions  How is token usage calculated?  Tokens are pieces of text that models process. How many tokens the same text produces depends on the model's tokenizer, the language, and the type of content. Claude 4.7 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview use a newer tokenizer that produces approximately 30 percent more tokens for the same text than earlier models. To see how many tokens a request uses on a specific model, count it with token counting and that model's ID. Are there free tiers or trials?  New users receive a small amount of free credits to test the API. Contact sales for information about extended trials for enterprise evaluation. How do discounts stack?  Batch API and prompt caching discounts can be combined. For example, using both features together provides significant cost savings compared to standard API calls. See prompt caching pricing for how the multipliers interact. What payment methods are accepted?  Major credit cards are accepted for standard accounts. Enterprise customers can arrange invoicing and other payment methods. For additional questions about pricing, contact support@anthropic.com . Was this page helpful?   Ask Docs 

summary.text: 코드 과제를 첫 시도에서 해결한 비율인 DeepSWE는 Full 79.0%, Wonder 78.8%입니다. 장기 프로젝트 성공률 SWE-Marathon은 57.5%(xhigh) 대 53.1%(max)로 추론 설정도 다릅니다. 반면 검사의 95% 이상을 통과한 실행 비율인 ProgramBench는 59.0%로 Claude Opus 5.5의 70.5%보다 낮습니다. AA 종합 지수도 56점으로 Opus 58점보다 낮아 모든 항목에서 상위는 아닙니다.

explanation.title: 모델 개요와 이전 계열에서의 변화
explanation.lead: Wonder 계열은 Spark의 단순한 이름 변경이 아니라 새 기반 모델 계열로 발표됐습니다.

blocks.title: Spark에서 Wonder로
blocks.text: Meta는 Spark에서 구축한 학습, 확장 기반 위에 더 강한 모델을 만들고 긴 작업, 기억과 집중을 학습했다고 설명합니다. 공식 모델 목록은 Spark와 Wonder를 별도 모델로 제공합니다. 이전 계열 대비 정확한 개선율을 계산할 공통 Spark 평가 행은 이번 카드에 없으므로 경쟁 표에 임의 수치를 채우지 않았습니다.

blocks.title: Active Memory와 Active Focus
blocks.text: Active Memory는 대화에서 중요한 정보를 다시 찾아 유지하는 능력, Active Focus는 긴 작업 중 새 정보에 맞추어 접근을 조정하고 진행을 이어가는 능력이라는 Meta의 설명입니다. 학습 방향과 제공자의 기능 설명이며 외부 영구 데이터베이스나 무오류 실행을 보장하지 않습니다. Wonder는 API 모델, Muse Code는 이를 사용하는 개발 제품이고 Full은 그 제품의 일부 구독에서 제공하는 별도 상위 모델입니다.

explanation.title: 성능 비교 해석
explanation.lead: 동일 이름의 평가라도 측정 주체와 작업 환경이 다르면 점수 차이를 그대로 모델의 우열로 해석하기 어렵습니다.

blocks.title: 코드 평가의 측정 주체와 도구
blocks.text: DeepSWE 1.1은 91개 저장소, 5개 언어의 113개 작업에서 기능, 회귀 테스트를 평가하는 pass@1, 즉 첫 시도의 성공 비율입니다. 카드에서 Wonder 계열과 Opus는 Datacurve 측정, Astra는 OpenAI 자체 보고, Fable은 Anthropic 시스템 카드에서 가져옵니다. SWE-Marathon은 Abundant AI 결과를 인용하며 경쟁 모델에 Codex, Claude Code가 사용됐으므로 공통 Harness 비교가 아닙니다. Harness는 모델에 도구와 실행, 평가 환경을 연결하는 틀입니다. 이 행의 Full은 xhigh로 다른 max 결과와 설정도 다릅니다.

blocks.title: 프로그램 재구성과 기억 평가의 의미
blocks.text: ProgramBench는 준비 후 네트워크를 끄고 mini-swe-agent로 프로그램을 재구성합니다. 수치는 숨겨진 테스트의 95% 이상을 통과한 rollout의 비율이며 모든 테스트의 통과율을 뜻하지 않습니다. MemoryBench는 Meta 내부 평가로 64,000~100,000 토큰 길이의 대화에 방해 정보와 갱신된 사실을 섞고 LLM이 가중 기준으로 판정합니다. 백만 토큰 문맥 전체나 영구 기억을 검증한 점수가 아닙니다.

blocks.title: 컴퓨터 조작과 종합 지표
blocks.text: OSWorld V2.1은 108개 Ubuntu 데스크톱 작업을 평가합니다. 평균 부분 점수와 완전 완료율은 별개이며 Opus는 제공자 보고 부분 점수만 있어 완료율을 미공개로 남겼습니다. Terminal-Bench와 AA Intelligence Index는 카드가 인용한 Artificial Analysis 결과입니다. AA 지수는 여러 평가를 묶은 점수이고 정답률이 아닙니다. 원 실행 기록 전체를 독립 대조한 것은 아닙니다. 카드 자체도 가능한 타사, 제공자 결과를 활용하고 그 외에는 내부, 자체 보고, 공식 순위 중 높은 검증 결과를 선택한다고 설명합니다.

explanation.title: 장점
explanation.lead: 평가 결과와 제공 조건에서 확인되는 상대적 강점을 정리했습니다.

blocks.title: 장기 코드 평가에서 높은 수치
blocks.text: 선택한 카드 비교군에서 Full의 DeepSWE 성공률 79.0%와 SWE-Marathon 성공률 57.5%는 가장 높습니다. 일반 Wonder보다 각각 0.2%포인트와 4.4%포인트 높아 긴 코드 작업을 강조하는 출시 방향과 부합합니다. 다만 전자는 출처가 혼재하고 후자는 xhigh 예외와 경쟁 제품 Harness 차이가 있으므로 두 차이를 동일 설정에서 입증한 개선 폭으로 단정하지 않습니다.

blocks.title: 일반 Wonder보다 넓어진 강점
blocks.text: ProgramBench 기준 충족 실행 비율은 Full 59.0%로 Wonder 50.0%, Astra 52.5%, Fable 55.5%보다 높습니다. Terminal-Bench 정확도도 Full 57.1%로 Wonder 52.0%보다 높습니다. 상위 모델의 개선을 보여주는 항목이지만 Opus의 70.5%와 59.6%보다 낮아 코드 작업 전체의 최우수라는 결론은 나오지 않습니다.

explanation.title: 단점과 한계
explanation.lead: 반대 결과와 접근 제약도 모델 선택의 근거에 포함했습니다.

blocks.title: 상위 모델이 항상 더 높지는 않음
blocks.text: MemoryBench 가중 점수는 Full 85.5로 Wonder 85.6보다 낮습니다. AA 지수 56점은 Opus 58점보다 낮고 OSWorld 부분 점수 78.4도 Fable 80.7과 Opus 81.8보다 낮습니다. Full의 OSWorld 완전 완료율 39.4% 역시 Fable 43.1%보다 낮습니다. DeepSWE의 0.2%포인트 차이는 표만으로 통계적 유의성이나 실제 프로젝트 개선을 입증하지 못합니다.

blocks.title: API 접근과 비용 비교의 제약
blocks.text: 공개 Model API가 없으므로 API 시스템에 직접 넣을 후보로 일반 Wonder와 같은 조건으로 볼 수 없습니다. 월 구독료에는 사용량, 제품 접근 조건이 묶여 있어 API 토큰 가격으로 환산할 근거가 부족합니다. Full의 Muse Code 최대 출력과 별도 PDF 지원도 이번 확인 범위에서는 명시된 수치를 찾지 못했습니다.

explanation.title: 가격과 제공 조건
explanation.lead: 표준 토큰 단가와 구독 플랜은 서로 다른 결제 단위입니다.

blocks.title: Wonder와 경쟁 API의 가격 차이
blocks.text: Wonder의 백만 토큰당 표준 입력 요금은 4달러, 출력 요금은 20달러로 Opus 5.5와 같습니다. Astra와 Fable의 기본 입력 10달러, 출력 50달러보다 낮지만 이전 Spark 1.3의 입력 1.25달러, 출력 4.25달러보다는 높습니다. 이는 해당 요금 항목의 비교이며 특정 작업이 같은 토큰량이나 같은 정확도로 끝난다는 뜻은 아닙니다. Astra는 입력이 272K 토큰을 초과하면 전체 요청의 입력과 캐시 요금을 2배, 출력 요금을 1.5배로 과금합니다. Meta에는 장문 할증이 없고 Fable과 Opus의 기본 1M 토큰 문맥도 장문 할증이 없습니다.

blocks.title: 추론과 도구 과금
blocks.text: Wonder의 내부 추론 토큰도 출력 요금에 포함됩니다. Meta 웹 검색은 검색 질의 1,000개당 2.50달러를 별도 청구합니다. 캐시 읽기 단가는 입력 전체에 적용되는 할인율이 아니며 캐시에서 실제 재사용한 부분에만 적용됩니다. 가격표의 출력 단가만으로 실제 답변 길이, 추론량, 검색량과 실행 시간을 알 수 없습니다.

blocks.title: Full 구독과 데이터 사용
blocks.text: Full은 Muse Code의 Power 플랜에서 월 50달러, Maximum 플랜에서 월 200달러에 제공합니다. Everyday 플랜 대비 Power는 20배, Maximum은 80배의 사용량을 제공하며, 이는 모델 성능 배수나 고정 토큰 수, 무제한 사용량을 뜻하지 않습니다. 구독은 Contributor mode가 기본으로 켜져 있어 더 많은 사용량을 받는 대신 프롬프트, 코드, 파일, 문맥, 응답을 향후 Meta 모델 학습에 사용할 수 있습니다. 끄면 이후 콘텐츠를 이 용도로 사용하지 않으며 과거 콘텐츠의 소급 삭제를 보장하는 설명은 아닙니다. Standard mode 콘텐츠는 학습에 사용하지 않는다고 명시합니다. 구독 전용 자격과 추가 PAYG 키의 청구는 분리되며 추가 키가 Full API 접근을 열지는 않습니다.

result.title: 장기 코드 평가의 상위 후보이지만 API, 종합 성능에서는 조건이 남습니다

points.label: 성능의 위치
points.text: Full은 일반 Wonder보다 여러 코드 평가에서 높지만 ProgramBench, AA, 컴퓨터 조작에서는 Opus, Fable에 뒤지는 항목이 있습니다.

points.label: 선택 조건
points.text: Muse Code의 Full 접근과 구독 조건이 필요한 경우에 검토할 후보입니다. API가 필요한 경우 공개 API를 제공하는 Wonder, 경쟁 모델과 별도로 판단해야 합니다.

caveats.text: 이 자료는 공식 소개, 사양, 가격과 카드의 평가 원문을 비교한 분석입니다. 모델 실행이나 독립 평가를 수행하지 않았으며 전체 벤치마크, 안전성 부록, 지역 접근, 실제 청구를 모두 확인한 것은 아닙니다.
가중치 공개, 매개변수 수, 로컬 실행 메모리와 별도 배포 라이선스는 이번 범위에서 확인하지 않았습니다. 다른 Meta 모델의 조건을 그대로 적용하지 않습니다.
